title: The Loyalty Tax - Why Job Switchers Out-Earn Stayers Again

sources.title: Pay premium for job hopping narrows to record low
Climbing the employment ladder tough when bottom rung is broken

claims.claim: The Atlanta Fed's Wage Growth Tracker shows median wage growth for job switchers rose to 4.1% in June 2026, versus 3.4% for job stayers.
At the April 2022 peak of the Great Resignation, job switchers saw median raises of 16%, per ADP data.
By early 2026 the pay premium for job hopping had narrowed to a record low.
The wage premium for job switchers rebounded significantly through the first quarter of 2026.

scenes.narration: In 2022, changing jobs paid a sixteen percent raise. Then the premium died. This year, it came back.

packaging.instagramCaption:
The 'loyalty tax' is back. 💸

Atlanta Fed data, June 2026: pay for job SWITCHERS grew 4.1% - stayers got just 3.4%.

The timeline matters —

🔸 2022: switchers peaked at 16% median raises
🔸 2024-25: the premium collapsed to a record low
🔸 2026: it's back

The lesson isn't 'always quit.' It's that new-hire pay reprices fast while incumbent pay lags. Loyalty is not a pay strategy - leverage is.

When did you last check your market price? 👇

Source: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, Wage Growth Tracker
